synopsis: The corpus recommends building a measured, independently reviewed credibility envelope before the prototype arrives, and substituting virtual for physical evidence only within that envelope [f71, f10466, f72, f10467]. Across credibility frameworks, this requires a defined use, risk-scaled effort, verification, physical validation, quantified uncertainty and independent review; physical tests anchor the model and confirm boundaries and influential changes [f186, f7536]. Validation does not automatically transfer across sites, weather, machine models or sensor positions: extensions require similarity arguments plus bridging evidence, while replay proves only conditions actually recorded [f614, f7569, f95, f5241]. Neural reconstruction illustrates the extrapolation risk: Para-Lane (2025) reports PSNR falling from 22.99 to 17.05 dB between recorded and adjacent lanes, while MV² (August 2026) reports 29.13 dB at drone height versus 10.36 dB from a car [f3707, f3709]. The planning gap is substantial: the organization reviewed lacks a documented credibility assessment, defined use envelope and validation against reality, and published operating limits were not found for several commercial precedents [f10414, f1656, f1660, f1666].
